h1: Getting signage permission for a brewpub front
title: Brewpub Signage Permission in India | Craft Beer School
desc: How to get permission for a brewpub sign: landlord consent, local body rules, alcohol advertising limits and what to put in the application.
teaser: The sign is the last thing you order and the first thing a customer sees. Plan its permission early.
standfirst: Signage looks like a design job and turns out to be a permissions job. A brewpub front touches the landlord, the local body and sometimes the excise rules on alcohol advertising. Here is the order to work in.
sections: Start with the landlord, then the building

Before you draw a sign, read the lease. It usually says what you may fix to the facade, who pays for damage and whether the landlord must approve the design. In a mall, a business park or a housing complex the management often has its own signage guidelines with a fixed zone, height and style. Those guidelines override your preferences.

If the building is a rented floor in a residential or mixed-use area, also check whether the owners' association or society has a say. Get every consent in writing. A verbal yes from a property manager is no use when a new manager arrives.

In most cities a sign facing a public road needs permission from the municipal corporation or the local body. The usual areas of control are the size, the height above ground, how far the sign projects over the footpath, the method of fixing and whether it is lit. Fees, forms and timelines differ by city and they change, so read the current rules for your local body or ask a licensing adviser.

Hanging boards over a public road are often the strictest category. A flat sign inside the shopfront line is usually the simplest to approve. If your brewpub is in a heritage zone or on a protected street, expect extra conditions on materials and colour.

This is where a brewpub differs from a cafe. India has strict limits on alcohol advertising. Some states and local bodies extend them to premises signage. A sign that names your brewpub is generally treated differently from a sign that advertises a beer brand or shows a product image. Rules vary by state and change, so ask the excise office or your adviser what you may show.

Plan for a cautious design. Put the brewpub name and a plain description such as "brewery and kitchen" on the main board. Keep brand slogans, pack images and any suggestion of a promotion off it until you know the rule. Our guide on the microbrewery licence in India shows how this connects to the licence you already need.

Have these ready before you submit:

  • A scaled drawing of the facade with the sign marked: width, height, depth and the height of its lower edge above the pavement.
  • The fixing method and a structural note if it is heavy or projecting.
  • Lighting details: type, wattage and whether it flashes or changes colour.
  • The landlord's or building's consent letter.
  • Your trade licence or shop registration. Add your brewing or bar licence where the office asks for it.

A drawing from your sign maker is better than a mock-up on a photo. It lets the officer check dimensions without guessing.

A sign is a structure. A large lit board on a first floor facade takes wind load on every monsoon gust, so ask the sign maker for the fixing method and the load it was designed for. Run the electrical feed in conduit with a proper isolator and an earthed frame. Keep the sign away from the exhaust of your kitchen and brewhouse, because grease and steam coat a board within a season. Building and fire approvals matter here too. Our guide on fire safety NOC and building approvals for a new brewpub covers what else the building needs.
Build the permission into your timeline

Signage approval can take weeks. The sign itself takes weeks to make. Founders who start after the fit-out ends open with a banner on a pole. Add signage to the project timeline next to the licence and the kitchen. If your opening date depends on getting a sign up, start the landlord letter and the drawing in the first month of the lease.

While you wait, ask whether a temporary banner is allowed and for how long. Many local bodies treat banners as a separate permission with its own limit on days.

This week, read the signage clause in your lease. Then ask your landlord for the building's signage guidelines and write down three things: the zone you may use, the maximum size and who approves the design. With those three answers you can brief a sign maker properly and avoid drawing something nobody can approve.
faqs: Do I need permission for a sign on my own shop?
In most cities, yes. A sign facing a public road usually needs local body permission as well as the landlord's consent. Rules differ by city, so check your local body.
Can a brewpub sign show beer brands?
Often not freely. Alcohol advertising is restricted. Some states extend that to signage. A sign with the premises name is usually safer. Check with the excise office or an adviser.
What drawing do I need for the application?
A scaled drawing of the facade with the sign's width, height, depth, lower edge height, fixing method and lighting details. Most offices prefer this to a photo mock-up.
Can I put up a temporary banner before the sign is approved?
Sometimes, for a limited number of days. Many local bodies treat banners as a separate permission. Ask before you hang one.
